parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
For $Q$: $-2mg\sin\alpha-F=2ma$, giving $-16m-7.2m=2ma$; and $R=2mg\cos\alpha=12m$. M1: Apply Newton's second law along or perpendicular to the plane to particle $Q$. Must use values for $\alpha$, $\sin\alpha$ or $\cos\alpha$. A1: Both correct.

$F=0.6(2mg\cos\alpha)=0.6(0.6)(20m)=7.2m$, so $2ma=-2mg(0.8)-0.6(2mg)(0.6)$. M1: Use $F=0.6R$, where $R$ is a component of $2mg$ only.

Acceleration of $Q$ up the plane while moving up the plane: $a=-11.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. A1 AG.

Total: 4 marks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
For $P$: $mg\sin\alpha-0.6R=ma$, giving $8m-3.6m=ma$, with $R=mg\cos\alpha=6m$ and $a=4.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. M1: Apply Newton's second law to attempt to find the acceleration of $P$. Must use values for $\alpha$ or $\sin\alpha$.

$Q$ comes to rest when $10-11.6T_1=0$, so $T_1=25/29=0.862$. M1: Use constant-acceleration equations to attempt to determine when $v_Q=0$.

For $P$, $s_{P\,(\mathrm{down})}=\dfrac12(4.4)T_1^2=1.635$. For $Q$, $s_{Q\,(\mathrm{up})}=10T_1+\dfrac12(-11.6)T_1^2=4.31$. M1: Use constant-acceleration equations to attempt to find either displacement at time $T_1$.

$d=6.4-s_{P\,(\mathrm{down})}-s_{Q\,(\mathrm{up})}=0.455$, then find $T_2=0.12$ using $d=s_{P2}-s_{Q2}=(4.4T_1)T_2+\dfrac12(4.4)T_2^2-\dfrac12(4.4)T_2^2$. M1: Attempt to find the extra distance $d$ needed to reach $6.4\,\mathrm{m}$ and use $u_P=4.4T_1$ at $T_1$ to find $T_2$. Here $s_{P2}$ and $s_{Q2}$ are distances travelled in time $T_2$.

Time before collision $=T_1+T_2=0.862+0.12=0.982\,\mathrm{s}$. A1. Official value $0.98194357\ldots$.

Alternative method: Use the same $P$ acceleration and $T_1$ results for the first two M1 marks. Then $s_{P\,(\mathrm{down})}=\dfrac12(4.4)t^2$ and $s_{Q\,(\mathrm{up})}=10T_1+\dfrac12(-11.6)T_1^2-\dfrac12(4.4)(t-T_1)^2$. M1: Use constant-acceleration equations to attempt to find either displacement at total collision time $t$. Set $\dfrac12(4.4)t^2+10T_1+\dfrac12(-11.6)T_1^2-\dfrac12(4.4)(t-T_1)^2=6.4$ and solve for $t$. M1. Time before collision $t=0.982\,\mathrm{s}$. A1; official value $0.98194357\ldots$.

Special case for candidates who do not take account of $Q$ coming to rest and changing direction: obtain $a_P=4.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. M1. Use $s_{P\,(\mathrm{down})}=(\pm)\dfrac12(4.4)t^2$ and $s_{Q\,(\mathrm{up})}=(\pm)10t+\dfrac12(-11.6)t^2$. M1: Attempt either displacement. Set $(\pm)s_P+(\pm)s_Q=6.4$, giving $\dfrac12(4.4)t^2+10t+\dfrac12(-11.6)t^2=6.4$, and solve a three-term quadratic for at least one solution. M1. Time $t=1\,\mathrm{s}$. A1; must reject $t=16/9$. Maximum 4 out of 5 marks.

Total: 5 marks.

parts.label: (c)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$u_{P\,(\mathrm{down})}=0+4.4(0.982)=4.3208$. B1 FT: Allow $\pm4.4$; follow through their $4.4$ and $0.982$.

$u_{Q\,(\mathrm{down})}=4.4(0.12)=0.528$. B1 FT: Allow $\pm4.4$; follow through their $4.4$ and $0.12$.

$\pm m(4.3208)\pm2m(0.528)=\pm(m+2m)v$. M1: Apply conservation of momentum, four terms, using their $u_P$ and $u_Q$ with $m$ and $2m$ respectively. The velocities after impact must be equal. Correct equation: $m(4.3208)+2m(0.528)=\pm(m+2m)v$.

Speed immediately after impact $=v=1.79\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. A1. Must be positive.

Special case for candidates who do not take account of $Q$ coming to rest and changing direction: $u_{P\,(\mathrm{down})}=0+4.4(1)=4.4$. B1 FT: Allow $\pm4.4$, following through their $1$ and $4.4$. $u_{Q\,(\mathrm{up})}=10-11.6(1)=-1.6$, so $u_{Q\,(\mathrm{down})}=1.6$. B1 FT: Allow $\pm(10-11.6(1))$, following through their $1$. Then $\pm m(4.4)\pm2m(1.6)=\pm(m+2m)v$. M1: Apply conservation of momentum, four terms, using their velocities with $m$ and $2m$ respectively; final velocities equal. Speed $v=2.53\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. A1. Allow $v=38/15$; must be positive.

Total: 4 marks.
